01 / The experience

A little world.
Made for them.

Tap a picture to explore. Try the microphone. The Home icon opens Math and Stories.

Tap inside the Watch. Swipe around it to look closer.

02 / Knowledge packs

A little discovery.
Ready to go.

A small picture shelf gives curiosity a place to start. Prepared discoveries offer something to explore on the go.

Why a small shelf?

Recognizable pictures make choosing easier before fluent reading. A saved discovery has its own place, so a child can return without starting over. Downloaded discovery cards use prepared content and narration.

03 / Ask Trustin

One question.
A new direction.

Tap the microphone to try a sample question, then choose where the conversation goes.

Scripted sample. No microphone is recorded.

Why three next steps?

Scaffolded learning means just enough help for the next step, then room to try. A short answer offers a foothold. Three clear prompts give the child an approachable next choice. This preview includes two prompt rounds, then returns to Curiosity; that shortened ending is for the website.

04 / Your guidance

Your family.
Your say.

Try how a parent’s choice can shape a response.

Illustrative topic control. Essential protections stay in place.

05 / Word help

A word to try. A story to keep.

Tap any word. Hear it, break it into sounds, or discover its meaning. Tap outside the bubble to return.

Why keep help on the page?

A small bubble preserves the picture and the child’s place in the story. Swipe inside the bubble to move between words. The prepared web sample plays individual words from the original page narration.

06 / Math

A little project.
Five small steps.

Choose an answer. Ask for a hint. Keep going at your own pace.

How does the challenge grow?

The first two Math bands use three answer choices. Later bands can use number entry with plus/minus controls and a keypad. Parents can change the starting point in Learning & reading. The next new project uses it; unfinished work stays saved.

07 / Their little world

A little choice.
All their own.

Open the shop. Try something on. Choose it with sample Stars, then wear it home.

Earned, never bought.

The backpack is optional. Try-on spends nothing, and choosing an item asks for confirmation. Parents can switch rewards off. The app caps earnings at 25 Stars a day, with no streak penalties. This preview includes 18 sample Stars and a small catalogue selection.

Scripted preview · No live AI or microphone capture · Privacy details

Parent Dock · iPhone

Their wonder. Your guidance.

01 / Overview

Their day.
At a glance.

Questions, Math and Stories in one calm view. Choose a child and a date range.

Why it’s designed this way

The overview gives each activity equal space. Counts open the underlying records, so a parent can move from a quick glance to the actual exchange. A visible update time makes the information’s freshness clear.

Counts describe saved activity, not a child’s ability. Offline discovery listening is not included.

02 / Activity

See the words.
Keep the context.

Read a question and its answer. Look back at Math practice or a finished story.

Why it’s designed this way

Filters and search help you find a particular moment without reading everything. Math separates independent work from supported practice. Individual records have a confirmed delete action. Learning records are for family reports and learning support, with no commercial profiling.

These are fictional records. Deleting a sample changes only this preview.

03 / Learning pace

A starting point.
Room to grow.

Choose a Math band and a small step within it. The next new project starts there.

Why it’s designed this way

Seven reference bands each have three steps. The first two bands use three answer choices, without division or sharing. Later work can use number entry. An explicit parent adjustment applies to the next new project; unfinished work, practice history and Stars stay intact.

The app adapts from practice evidence over time. This website uses prepared examples and does not assess a child.

04 / Reading

A little help.
Right there.

Set the reading pace. On the Watch, a tap on a word opens Hear, Sounds and Meaning.

Why it’s designed this way

Word help stays in a small bubble over the story, so the child keeps their place. They can move between words and tap outside to return. Reading speed has a playable sample before you save your choice. Downloaded books remain available offline.

The web example uses the original Pip story and narration. Word explanations are prepared text; Hear plays a word from the recorded page.

05 / Safeguards

Your family.
Your guidance.

Choose how supported topics are handled. Essential protections always remain in place.

Why it’s designed this way

Topic preferences name their consequence: an age-appropriate explanation, a conversation with a grown-up, or no discussion. Learning, reading, explanation style and rewards have their own clearly named settings. Parent choice cannot authorize harmful instructions or commercial persuasion.

Questions about being hurt or feeling unsafe retain supportive guidance toward a trusted adult. No AI safeguard is a guarantee.

06 / Explanation style

Help that
makes sense.

Choose shorter sentences, familiar examples or a calmer explanation style.

Why it’s designed this way

A bounded choice is easier to understand than an open-ended instruction box. The parent can see what will change, then save. Scaffolded learning means providing enough help for the next step, with room for the child to try.

These choices shape supported AI explanations. They do not rewrite the wording of illustrated books.

07 / Stars & appearance

Their little world.
Your choice.

Stars can unlock outfits and places. You decide whether rewards are enabled.

Why it’s designed this way

The backpack is an optional destination. Try-on does not spend Stars; choosing an item requires a separate confirmation. Stars are earned through learning, with a daily limit of 25. They cannot be bought with money. Wishes do not expire and there are no streak penalties.

This demo begins with 18 sample Stars and a small selection from the native catalogue. No payment or real account is involved.

08 / Watch setup

Connected.
On your terms.

Connect a child’s profile to the paired Watch. Review access or disconnect it.

Why it’s designed this way

A child profile and a Watch’s access are separate choices. Paired access remains available until revoked. Disconnect explains its scope before confirmation: it stops future server access, without unpairing Apple devices or deleting the parent account.

The current beta uses a Watch normally paired with an iPhone. Apple Family Setup is not supported. This website never connects to a device.
